place.zh: 石坳村 · 屋后柴垛 · 半夜

setup.zh: 它一整天没醒，尾根的断口渗着银色的血。半夜里，它睁开了一只眼睛。你问她：真的有仙人？
setup.en: It has not woken all day; silver blood seeps from the cuts at its tail. At midnight it opens one eye. You ask her: are there really immortals?

recap.zh: 半夜里银月醒了一会儿：仙人是真的，凡人能修，一万个里不到一个——「剩下的，去问他们。」
recap.en: At midnight Yinyue woke a while: immortals are real, mortals can cultivate, fewer than one in ten thousand — "The rest, ask them."

zh: 柴垛上，一团凉冰冰的银毛。
断口渗出的血，是银的，像落了一层霜。
半夜，它睁开了一只眼睛。
en: On the woodpile, a cold curl of silver fur.
The blood from its cuts is silver, like a fall of frost.
At midnight, it opens one eye.

story.zh:
那天夜里，你把"围脖"抱到屋后柴垛上。

它一整天都没醒。身子是凉的，那一条尾巴垂着，尾根上那八道断口，又渗出了血——银色的，一滴一滴落在柴草上，像下了一层霜。

你守到半夜。

半夜里，它睁开了一只眼睛。

⟪**银月**：……吵死了。你喘气那么大声干什么。⟫

你松了一口气。松得太猛，差点哭出来。你憋住了。

**你**：银月。你说你是从仙界掉下来的。

⟪**银月**：嗯。⟫

**你**：仙界在哪？

⟪**银月**：上面。⟫

**你**：比蒙山顶还高？

⟪**银月**：高多了。⟫

**你**：那你掉下来的时候，疼不疼——

⟪**银月**：（一尾巴拍在你嘴上）一个一个问。⟫

你想了想。有一个问题，你从谷底憋到现在，憋了一整天。

**你**：你说你只剩「金丹」了。金丹……是金子做的丹吗？

⟪**银月**：……⟫

**你**：值钱吗？比鹿皮值钱吗？能换几斤肉？

⟪**银月**：（闭上了眼睛）本王不想醒了。⟫

**你**：还有「修为」。修为是什么？能吃吗？

⟪**银月**：不能。⟫

**你**：那「修仙」呢？是修房子的一种吗？

⟪**银月**：……⟫

**你**：修仙人？仙人坏了，要人修？

银月把脸埋进了自己的尾巴里。好半天，没抬起来。

⟪**银月**：（闷闷地）好。好。本王从头说。⟫

她抬起头，看了看天上的月亮。

⟪**银月**：吴婆婆有没有讲过，蒙山顶上住过一个骑白鹤的老头？⟫

**你**：讲过！一顿饭吃一颗枣，活了八百岁。我爹说那是编的。

⟪**银月**：你爹说错了。⟫

你的嘴，慢慢张大了。

⟪**银月**：仙人，是真的。活八百岁的有，活八千岁的也有。骑鹤的，骑龙的，踩一片云就走的，都有。他们以前，也都是凡人——猎户，樵夫，种地的，读书的。后来学会了一样本事：把天地间的灵气，一点一点收进自己的身子里，炼成自己的东西。一年，十年，一百年。不老，不病，力能搬山，最后连天都关不住。⟫

⟪**银月**：这，就叫修仙。⟫

柴垛上很静。你听见自己的心，在咚咚地跳。

**你**：那……我也能？

⟪**银月**：能。但很难。一万个凡人里，能修的，不到一个。能修的人里，一百个，九十九个老死了事。⟫

**你**：那剩下那一个呢？

银月没有回答。她看着你，眼睛慢慢合上了一半。

⟪**银月**：……你还有一肚子要问的。本王知道。可本王，答不动了。⟫

**你**：那我问谁？

⟪**银月**：问他们。这世上有一群人，专门修仙，专门教人修仙。灵气是什么，丹田是什么，境界是什么——他们会告诉你。比本王，有耐心。⟫

她顿了一下。

⟪**银月**：……当然，没本王教得好。⟫
story.en:
That night you carry the "scarf" out to the woodpile behind the house.

It hasn't woken all day. Its body is cold, its one tail hangs limp, and the eight cuts at the root of it have started to bleed again — silver, drop by drop onto the straw, like a fall of frost.

You keep watch until midnight.

At midnight, it opens one eye.

⟪**Yinyue:** …So noisy. Why are you breathing so loud?⟫

You let out your breath. Let it out so hard you nearly cry. You hold it in.

**You:** Yinyue. You said you fell from the immortal realm.

⟪**Yinyue:** Mm.⟫

**You:** Where's the immortal realm?

⟪**Yinyue:** Up.⟫

**You:** Higher than the top of Mount Meng?

⟪**Yinyue:** Much higher.⟫

**You:** So when you fell, did it hurt —

⟪**Yinyue:** (slapping its tail over your mouth) One at a time.⟫

You think. There's one question you've been holding in since the bottom of the valley — a whole day.

**You:** You said all you've got left is a "Golden Core." A Golden Core… is it a pill made of gold?

⟪**Yinyue:** …⟫

**You:** Is it worth a lot? More than a deer hide? How many jin of meat would it buy?

⟪**Yinyue:** (closing its eyes) This king would rather not be awake.⟫

**You:** And "cultivation." What's cultivation? Can you eat it?

⟪**Yinyue:** No.⟫

**You:** Then "cultivating immortality"? Is that a kind of house repair?

⟪**Yinyue:** …⟫

**You:** Repairing immortals? Immortals break and need fixing?

Yinyue buries its face in its own tail. For a long time it doesn't come up.

⟪**Yinyue:** (muffled) Fine. Fine. This king will start from the beginning.⟫

It lifts its head and looks up at the moon.

⟪**Yinyue:** Has Granny Wu ever told you about an old man who lived on top of Mount Meng and rode a white crane?⟫

**You:** She has! One jujube a meal, and he lived eight hundred years. My father says it's made up.

⟪**Yinyue:** Your father is wrong.⟫

Slowly, your mouth falls open.

⟪**Yinyue:** The immortals are real. Some live eight hundred years, some eight thousand. Crane-riders, dragon-riders, ones who step onto a cloud and go — all of them. Every one of them was a mortal once — hunters, woodcutters, farmers, scholars. Then they learned one thing: to gather the spirit qi of heaven and earth into their bodies, bit by bit, and refine it into something that is theirs. One year, ten years, a hundred. No ageing, no sickness, strong enough to move mountains — until in the end not even heaven can hold them.⟫

⟪**Yinyue:** That is what cultivating immortality means.⟫

It is very quiet on the woodpile. You can hear your own heart, thumping.

**You:** Then… could I?

⟪**Yinyue:** You could. But it's hard. Of ten thousand mortals, fewer than one can cultivate at all. Of those who can, ninety-nine in a hundred grow old and die with nothing to show.⟫

**You:** And the one left over?

Yinyue doesn't answer. It looks at you, and its eyes slowly close halfway.

⟪**Yinyue:** …You've got a bellyful more to ask. This king knows. But this king… can't answer any more.⟫

**You:** Then who do I ask?

⟪**Yinyue:** Them. In this world there are people who do nothing but cultivate, and teach others to. What spirit qi is, what a dantian is, what the realms are — they'll tell you. More patiently than this king.⟫

It pauses.

⟪**Yinyue:** …Not as well as this king, of course.⟫
